LESSON 1
GOD’S RIGHT TO COMMAND
Scripture Texts: Exodus 20:1-2; Leviticus 18:1-5; Joshua 24:20-24; John 14:8-15
The fact of the Creation gives God the right to demand that we obey Him. But
God does not use His divine power to force man to obey Him. The free choice of
man is part of the divine plan for this world. God has the right to place
commandments before His Creation. God’s Laws are not given to be a hindrance,
but to help mankind. What does it matter whether we build our living on the Law of
God or on the principle of doing as we please? How can we know, without trying
both ways ourselves, whether it is better to do as we please, or to do as God
commands?
We have but to read our newspapers and listen to the newscasts to see judgment
at work. Our eyes are opened to the world situation, and the truth comes home to us
that “he who will not be ruled by God will be ruled by tyrants.”
MEMORY VERSE: If ye love me, keep my commandments.—John 14:15
God Is His Own Authority
Exodus 20:1-2 And God spake. When God speaks, it is the Word of authority.
How blessed we are that God does communicate! In old times He spoke to holy men, and what He said to them
helps us know Him better. God chose to reveal Himself to man in every age. I am the Lord thy God. We have
here God’s own affirmation of complete authority. He is the one and only true God, besides Whom there is no
other, a jealous God forbidding His chosen ones – the Hebrews – to seek after any other god or to question His
own claim upon them. God is Lord and Master. He has never changed in any age. He requires the same of us,
His new Israel. Which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt. Israel must never forget that its
deliverance had been brought by God, not by human means; nor does He want us to forget.
Past Experience Encourages Future Obedience
Leviticus 18:1-5 After the doings of the land of Canaan. The exodus from Egypt was to lead Israel into
Canaan. What is their gain if they merely exchange one slavery for another? God wills that His people have a
real deliverance, entire and complete. He warns them of the temptations and idolatries lying in wait for their new
home. Spiritual decay, which had so cursed them in Egypt, must never raise its ugly head in the Land of
Promise. As it is with freedom, so it is with pure religion – the cost of both is obedience, vigilance, and effort.
Ye shall do my judgments…ordinances…statutes. We see clearly that God’s requirement is obedience to His
Word. As for the ways of Canaan, Israel was not to do them, not to walk in them. Israel was to do…keep… and
walk in the righteous ways of the Lord. Notice how closely God identifies Himself with those commands,
saying “my statutes,” “my judgments,” “mine ordinances,” as opposed to “their ordinances.”
Absolute rejection of Canaan’s idolatry and absolute obedience of His supreme will was God’s command to
Israel. In a world where no absolutes are the basis teaching, the Lord God still commands these same absolutes
for His people. Absolute rejection of all the gods of this world and absolute acceptance of, and obedience to, the
Lord of lords, and King of kings, and only true God.
An Individual Choice
Joshua 24:20-24 We will serve the Lord. When man was created in the image of God, it was this moral
righteousness that differentiated him from the rest of the animal world. He was given the freedom to choose

God’s way or to follow the way of disobedience. If man would forsake the Lord, He would do him no hurt. If
man would honor God and keep His commandments and walk in His ways, then man could be assured of God’s
blessing and of His abiding presence. The promises of God are always conditional. God’s benefits are freely
given to those who obey, but His judgments are reserved for those who disobey. The Lord our God will we
serve. Thus the covenant became a seal binding them to God’s holiness and freeing them to grow into the
Godlike image in which they had been created.
What happened to a nation also happens in the lives of individuals. The gods of the world clamor so loudly
for our worship, and the way of sin is made so attractive that we are constantly being pulled in two directions.
The choice is left to each of us. God’s grace is sufficient for us.
God Reveals Himself Through His Son
John 14:8-15 I am in the Father, and the Father in me. It is proper that we bring this lesson to a climax in
the New Testament, and most particularly, with the Words of Jesus, God’s Son.
When God sent His Son into the world to redeem the world, He sent Him with only one price, His life.
When God sent His Son to conquer sin, He sent Him with only one weapon, a sinless life. With this weapon, He
conquered, breaking the power of sin and restoring man to the divine relationship. The highest ideal and
authority possible is this of God in Christ reconciling the world to Himself. He purchased each soul, and His
ownership gives Him complete right to command. Christ’s commandments are not grievous, but are a blessing
and are of a great advantage to those who love and obey them. God gave commandments not to punish or to
restrict us, but because He loves us and wants us to enjoy the full life. Whose commands are you obeying?
If ye love me, keep my commandments. The issue is that simple. God has always received much lip
service; missing has been heart service. Love responds to loyal, spontaneous obedience. Obedience was the
requirement for ancient Israel and is no less essential to the Christian today.
JUST A THOUGHT
“The judgment is that a man has to choose, and that he chooses as he does,
and that he gets what he has chosen, and ends up chained to it.”

God – the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit – created all
things. First, God created inorganic matter; then, organic
or living matter – plants and animals. To each He gave
the laws which were to govern their existence. Last, He
created man in His own image, different from any other
being, and gave him dominion over all other living things

work and saw it was very good.
We should take this seriously. We take our jobs

MEMORY VERSE: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.—Genesis 1:1
The Creator
Genesis 1:1-19 The Bible starts at the beginning with God. The beginning is as far back to a source as one
can go. It starts at the beginning with a supreme, all-powerful Being. There must be such a One before there can
be an orderly, organized universe. Created – He made all things out of nothing. He brought into existence that
which did not exist before. Only God can do this. Man can make things by putting them together in different
combinations than they were before. But man must have material to start with – material created by God. Read
Hebrews 11:3. The Spirit of God moved. The Trinity worked together in creation – the Father, the Son, and
the Holy Spirit. Read John 1:1-3; Colossians 1:16-17; Hebrews 1:2; Hebrews 1:10-12 to see that Christ took
part in it.
Let there be light: and there was light. God alone can successfully say, “Let there be …” First, God
created inorganic matter, that is, things without life. Here is recorded the creation of light, darkness, day, night,
and the firmament (sky), and the placing of the clouds, rivers, seas, and dry land. All of this had to be before
organic things, or those things with life could not live. The first organic things made were plant life. It was
good. This is repeated several times. Man works by trial and error. God’s work is perfect. There were no flaws
in things as first created. After his kind – Each thing was to bring forth after its kind – always produce after
itself. Beans produce beans; cattle produce cattle – never otherwise. God laid down laws in creation which are
continually operating. Basically, they are as follows: (1) The young of all plants and animals are after their kind.
(2) The heavenly bodies move in ordered courses. (3) Man has dominion over the other living things on the
earth. (4) Vegetation is for food. If these were recognized by all, we would not have the evolution theory. On the
fourth day God created the heavenly bodies, the sun, moon, and stars, and set them moving in their appointed

THE CREATION OF MAN
Scripture Text: Genesis 2:7-24
Continuing the study of the Creation, we find in
Genesis, Chapter 2, details of what was briefly told
in Chapter 1.
Man was different from the beasts. He was made
of two things – the dust of the ground and the breath
of life. The breath from God made him a living soul.
The first woman was made from the first man’s rib,
thus making her of the same substance and nature as
man. Since all people came from this first pair, all of
us are from one human family with the same nature
and position before God. All are souls. God placed Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden, establishing the home.
He gave them one negative command – not to eat of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. Eating would bring

MEMORY VERSE: And so it is written, the first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made
a quickening spirit.—1 Corinthians 15:45
Something Eternal
Genesis 2:7 Of the dust of the ground. At first, man was not worth much, just a dust man, his body made
of the earthly elements. Then, that wonderful moment – one of the greatest of all time – when the great Creator
stooped to put His breath, the breath of life, within the earthly body, and man became a living soul – a
priceless finished product. In that instant, something was added to man that placed him in a different class from
all the rest of Creation on earth. He alone received the breath of life, alone became a living soul. In that instant
began something that will never end. When the breath of the eternal God entered man, man became eternal too.
That soul can never end. It was living then; it could die (for it did), but could never cease to be.
Man was made in the image of God. God gave him intelligence, will, the power of choice, and conscience.
Within him were placed the emotions such as love, hope, sympathy, and mercy. He has the power of aspiration,
that is, to reach toward and attain the fulfillment of an ideal. He can form a plan and work towards its
achievement. He is a spiritual being, capable of fellowship with God, capable of being partaker of the divine
nature (2 Peter 1:4).
The human race is a unit; all came from the same beginning. All are children of Adam. The Bible tells us
that the human race is one – a unit. Genesis 3:20 speaks of the mother of all living. Acts 17:26 tells us that God

God Provided a Home
Genesis 2:8-17 And the Lord planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man… Only the
approximate location of Eden is known. Eden is situated in Armenia, near the origin of the rivers, Tigris and
Euphrates, and in which the same region rise the Araxes (Pison of Genesis) and the Oxus (Gihon).” – Smiths
Bible Dictionary. The Hiddekel is the modern Tigris.

Wouldn’t the world be drab? God provided for the whole man, giving attention to both the spiritual and
physical. He desires man’s highest good, his greatest possible joy. As the crowning furnishing of the garden

CREATION VERSUS EVOLUTION
(Part 1)
Scripture Texts: John 5:46-47; 1 Corinthians 15:39; Genesis 1:25-27;
Genesis 2:7
The Bible record of Creation should be sufficient to establish our belief
in its statement that God created man and the animals and plants by His
direct act and that they were first made in their completed form and in the
various species in which they continue in this present time. But the theory
of evolution has had such widespread teaching that it is embedded as an
accepted fact in much of our education and literature. Our children and
young people meet it continually, not always by name. Numberless souls
have been led to disbelieve God’s Word by it. Hence it is our duty to
establish faith by bringing the issues into the open and examining into their
truth or falsity.
Everything has a source. Every effect has a cause. Like begets like. All
truth agrees. These are basic truths to remember.
MEMORY VERSE: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and
female created he them.—Genesis 1:27
Moses’ Writing Inspired by God
John 5:46-47 Moses wrote Genesis that tells of creation. Jesus places the truth of Moses’ writings beyond
question when He gives them His approval. He links belief of them with belief of His own Words. In a very real
sense, Moses’ writings ARE Jesus’ Words. They were inspired by God, or given to Moses by God (2 Peter
1:21). We need fear no statement which is proven to be a fact. It will agree with all other truth, and so, with the
Bible.
Life is here. How did it come to be? There are three theories held.
1. Creation – Those who accept the Bible believe that life is of divine origin, that God created man and
each species of plants and animals in their completed form. There may be development within a species.
For instance, cattle have been improved for beef and for milk, but they are still cattle. But this is limited.
It cannot go beyond the boundary of its species, its kind. No new species has ever been formed. Since
this answer of how life came to be is in the Bible, it is not a theory, but a record. We believe it as God’s
Word,
2. Naturalistic Evolution – The evolution theory was set forth by Charles Darwin in his books, “Origin of
Species” in 1859 and “The Descent of Man” in 1871. The theory takes two forms. Naturalistic or
Materialistic Evolution teaches that life began spontaneously (of itself) as a cell in the slime of the ocean
bed, and by its own power worked upward through various advancing stages until the present state of
man was reached. In this process, all the forms of plant and animal life were produced. This theory
leaves God out.
3. Theistic Evolution – This is a modified form of the evolution theory that teaches that living things have
evolved, but it gives God a place in the plan. It is an attempt to reconcile the two schools of thought. It
teaches that God created the germ of life in the beginning. Then it evolved into the many forms we have
now. God is called the First Cause. Do not fear to investigate. To prove a false theory false, trace it to its
end. Truth cannot be overthrown. Truth is eternal.

Different Flesh
1 Corinthians 15:39 All flesh is not the same flesh. It would be the same if it all came from the same
beginning cells as theorized in evolution. It would not be if each kind were made by a separate act of creation.
God’s Word tells us here that the flesh of men, of beasts, of fish, and of birds are different kinds. Then they
cannot all have been the same thing in some distant past. They must have been created separately as the Bible
says.
Genesis 1:25 God made the beast … cattle … and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his
kind. The kind of each was established. Each was to follow its established pattern, or keep to its own kind. The
young of each was to be of the same kind as its parents. Ten times this chapter repeats after his kind (or their
kind), indicating its importance. This law of reproduction prohibits the change from one species to another; the
taking on of new parts, new characteristics, and new nature, which evolution says has happened continually.
Genesis 1:26-27 God created man in his own image – not in the image of a cell in the slime. No beast was
our father. What great favor God showed to this last piece of His creation to make him after the pattern of
Himself! No other animal was made thus. They all were to be after their kind, or after the pattern they were
made in. Man alone was after the likeness of God. Therefore, man cannot have come from beasts. Both men and
women were made the same, in the image of God, for male and female created he them.
Genesis 2:7 The breath of God made man a living soul. Of no other of creation is this said. The beasts are
not souls. Plants are not. Only man is. Being of a different kind than beasts, man could not have come from
them. He was created by God separately as the Bible says. He was a man or human when first made. He
continues ever since to be a man. Being made a living soul in the image of God, man was linked with God. Sin
spoiled the relationship, but still, we are made for God and can never be happy and complete without Him. The
unsaved person has an empty, hungry place that only God can fill.

The most wonderful thing ever made by man is a living for his family.

It is very important that we, as God’s creation, know the truth of our high
origin. Since the Bible account of the beginning of things is Gods eternal Word,
it is true.
The theory of evolution – that all life began by itself as simple cells and
evolved into all the forms of plants and animals and people – cannot also be true.
The theory of evolution of species is contrary to the Bible. We cannot believe
both. Jesus tells us that Moses’ writings, which record Creation, are true.
We have learned in the past lesson a few of the many reasons why the
evolution of species cannot have happened, that it is proven untrue.
MEMORY VERSE: He hath made everything beautiful in his time: also he
hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that
God maketh from the beginning to the end.—Ecclesiastes 3:11
Apostles Taught Creation
Colossians 1:16-17 For by him – God – were all things created…in heaven…in earth…all things were
created by him. Here Paul makes it very plain that the early Apostles believed and taught the report of creation
as recorded in Genesis. By him all things consist. God put together just the right consistency to make all things
just as He desired them to be in their finished state.
Faith in the Bible is Vitally Important
Hebrews 11:2-3 Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God… It
makes a great difference which is true, evolution or creation. If evolution were true, the Bible would not be. If
man evolved from a lowly state to a higher one, then the Bible account of his fall from a holy state to one of sin
would not be true. Not being a sinner, he would have no need of a Savior.
If a man’s origin was from a cell in the slime and up through the brute beasts, then he would not be
responsible to anyone for the quality of his life. But if, as the Bible says, man was created by God and in God’s
image, then we are responsible to God, and the Bible statement of a coming judgment is inescapable. Then man
needs a Savior.
Since man needs a Savior, any false theory, however good and beautiful it may appear, which binds him to
that fact and so prevents him from receiving one, is unspeakably bad.
Some Objections to Evolution
Webster defines evolution as follows: To evolve means to unfold or unroll, to open and expand. As to the
method by which the many animals and plants came to be, evolution is the theory that “all animals and plants
are the descendants of very few simple organisms, perhaps of but one, not unlike some of the simplest
protozoans existing now. The theory includes also the descent of man from the lower animals.” Now let us list a
few of the glaring errors in the theory of evolution of species.

1. Not Proven – The evolution theory is but a theory; that is, it is unproven. In two volumes of Darwin “we
may well suppose” is found more than 800 times. In contrast, the Bible account of creation is definite
and positive. In the first chapter of Genesis “it was so” is found five times.
2. Impossible – Life is here. It had to have a beginning, a source. If evolution were true, it would mean that
the first life was produced by inorganic matter. That has never happened and is impossible to happen. It
is much easier to believe that God created life.

of proof. No one has ever seen a form of life part way between one species and another. Genesis
Chapter 1, in the space of fifteen verses, ten times states Gods Law that both plant and animal life shall

what we know of man from history and from research indicates degeneracy, that is, that man fell from a
high physical, mental, and moral plane to a lower state. The really proved conclusions of science agree
with the Bible. Genesis tells of man coming from the hand of God perfect, then falling into sin.
Scientific investigation agrees with this, showing that people have gone from civilization to savagery,
rather than the other way.
6. No Missing Link Found – A few bones have been found at different places and times which
evolutionists claim to be those of beings part way between the ape and the man. There is no proof of
this. In November 1953 one such, a skull called the Piltdown Man, has been found to be a hoax. It was
discovered to be of a modern ape, scraped and treated with acid to appear human and old. Human skulls

THE PURPOSE OF MAN
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 43:7, Isaiah 43:21; Revelation 4:11; Psalm 8:3-6;
Psalm 24:1
We have learned of the creation of the world with its complex
organization, its elements, its many living plants and animals, with man as
the highest creation of all. Why did God make man? What is our purpose
here? Is it the pleasing of our desires, the drawing to ourselves some of the
earth’s substance, the gaining of notice from other human beings, drifting
with no effort, keeping busy, or helping others? Some may think this last is
the best purpose any life can serve. No, it is included in our duty, but the
essential purpose of our lives is much higher than that.
MEMORY VERSE: This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew
forth my praise.—Isaiah 43:21
You Are Not Your Own
Isaiah 43:7 God said of man, I have created him for my glory. To the Maker belongs the right of choosing
the use for His product. Man is to be part of the glory of God, to add to His glory.
Since God made man, man was made for God. The greatest thing we can ever do is to be a glory and praise
to Him and to give Him pleasure. This is first, a matter of BEING, then, of DOING. If we are a glory to God in
our hearts, acts will follow that will glorify Him. Each person is a soul with a life to live for God. Each has a
work to do that no other can do.
Dare we say, “It is my life; I will live it as I please?” If one makes no profession of Christianity, is he not
bound by the Christian standard? Does his nonprofession excuse his life? God made everyone for Himself. To
withhold service from Him is to not only to steal from Him, but to cheat yourself. When we thwart our highest
purpose, we crush hope for our greatest happiness.
We Owe God Glory and Praise
Isaiah 43:21 This people have I formed for myself. The intent of God was that people were for Himself.
He owns us. When Satan introduced sin to people, he was trespassing on God’s territory. He was stealing what
was not his. When we yield any of ourselves or our time to serve another than God, we are stealing from God.
We are here to shew forth His praise, which is giving Him glory. The glory is worth; the praise is
acknowledgment of that worth. Glory is light shining out; praise is the reflection of that light shining back upon
the source.
Is this primarily the fruit of our lips? Do we fulfill this purpose by speaking of God’s goodness, testifying of
His faithfulness, or praising Him in song and prayer? Certainly, this is part of it, but SPEAKING His glory is not
enough. We are to BE His glory. Being part of the body of Christ, saints are part of the glory of God. Insofar as

How to Give Glory and Praise
Revelation 4:11 All creation was created to please God, to bring Him pleasure. Since we were made for
that, we fulfill out highest possibility when we give Him the greatest pleasure of which we are capable.

THE BEGINNING OF SIN
Scripture Text: Genesis 3:1-7
Genesis is the book of beginnings. We have studied the beginnings
of the earth, plant, animal, and human life. We learned something of
their purpose, the reason for each being created.
Our lesson today deals with the beginning of sin and its dreadful
effects upon the human race. We have been studying about God and
man. In this week’s lesson, a new character appears upon the stage. Who
is he? Let us see what the Bible tells of his purpose.
MEMORY VERSE: And be sure your sin will find you out.
—Numbers 32:23b
Unbelief Opened the Door
Genesis 3:1-6 While the serpent was the agent or tool used to tempt Eve, we know that the source of
temptation was the devil. Satan wanted to spoil God’s creation. He knew what God’s command was and he went
to work, and he has never slacked off. Ye shall not surely die. This was a direct contradiction of God. He
brought a doubt to Eve’s mind as to whether God’s Word is true. Ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.
He mixed some truth into the lie which made it more dangerous. Eve was tempted to (1) disbelieve Gods Word;
(2) disobey God’s command; (3) doubt God’s goodness in thinking He selfishly withheld good from man; (4)
jealousy or envy of God, in wanting an ability God had; and (5) pride in thinking she could judge better than
God. These were sins of enormous proportion.
Verse 6 brings the awfulness of the entrance of sin into the world. Eve’s downfall was in listening, looking,
considering, and acting upon the temptation. Don’t say we would not have done so. Look rather at man’s easy
yielding to sin from then until now. We must be on our guard at all times. The devil shows the sweet and
beautiful side first – good for food … pleasant to the eyes … to make one wise. The bitter follows after.
Sin seems, at first, to be pleasant and to promise joy and reward. But always, always, death is joined
inseparably with sin. Death leads finally to the flames of hell. Did eat, and gave also unto her husband – Sin
spreads and sin grows. Sinners lead others to sin. As one succumbs to the tempter’s voice, disobedience follows
in quick succession. And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food – God had not said that it was
not good for food. Here we see temptation through the lust of the flesh. That it was pleasant to the eyes –
temptation through the lust of the eyes. To make one wise – temptation through the pride of life. These are the
three realms where man is most vulnerable to the attack of the evil one. The passions and appetites are always
being attacked by the Tempter. We are easily tempted to covet, because of its beauty or usefulness, that which is
not ours.
Their Eyes Opened
Genesis 3:7 Eyes … were opened – They knew good and evil. The knowledge immediately brought
problems, as it ever does. Knew that they were naked – innocence had fled. Made … aprons – Now they tried
to remedy matters. Man has been trying ever since to remedy sin’s damage. There is but one remedy.
In these verses we find a perfect description of the way sin works in the lives of people. First, there comes
the voice of doubt. If the devil can get us to doubt the Word of God as found in the Bible or as spoken to us by
God’s Spirit, or through our consciences, he has successfully started us on the downward path of sin. After
doubting the Word of God, it is an easy thing to deny it and to live as if it had never been spoken.

The opening of their eyes gave them more knowledge than that they were naked. They also knew they had
sinned. Now knowing right from wrong, they knew they were guilty. They knew good and evil. We have this
knowledge now. A child is not many years old when within him awakens this knowledge, and he knows when

it that still, small voice within us. If we will not override it and keep it tender, it will steer us away from those
things which lead us to be tempted to do wrong. Many temptations would never be presented to us if we did not
stand and look at the thing that we are not to have a part of. If Eve would have stayed away from the tree, the
fruit would not have tempted her.
Human Nature Then and Now
Adam and Eve believed a lie rather than the truth. Many believe a false doctrine with no Biblical proof, yet
question and doubt the truth. People will follow the downward way with no encouragement from anyone. If we
wish them to walk the way of God, we must put forth effort to encourage them constantly. Since this is the need,
let us lead and teach them to climb the way of God. How clearly here we see the frailty and weakness of human
nature. The strongest of us is so prone to fall when we lean to our own understanding.
When God lets us know that there are some things He wants us to let alone, do not try to figure out the
reason why. No matter how many good things we may think we see about them, when God says they are
forbidden, they will destroy your soul when you overstep God’s command. Constantly we must look to Jesus,
trusting His wisdom and never ourselves, obeying His warnings to watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into
temptation.
The truth that is being taught here is that the first man was tempted, and that he fell before the onslaughts of
the Tempter. Although life has become much more complicated since this story in Genesis was written, the
essentials remain the same.

Jesus did not come that we may live better but that we may live forever.

LESSON 8
THE FALL OF MAN
Scripture Text: Genesis 3:8-24
Adam and Eve were a glory to God for a time. They communed with
God. Their souls lived. Then the serpent, as the agent of Satan, tempted them
by a lie, a half-truth. They believed him, sinned, ate the fruit God had
forbidden. Immediately they knew they had sinned. Also, immediately their
souls died. They tried to hide from God. He found them and pronounced
punishment upon each. He drove them from the garden. He had a plan for
giving them life again.
MEMORY VERSE: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is
eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.—Romans 6:23
The Sinner Hides from God
Genesis 3:8-13 Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God. According to our
text, God is pictured walking in the garden here on earth, enjoying His handiwork, and communing with man,
the crown of His creation. But on this occasion, the man was nowhere to be found, for he knew he had sinned,
and so, he hid himself from God in shame and fear. Sin always makes us cowards. When we do something
wrong, we are afraid to face up to it and confess it. Guilt caused Adam and Eve to try to hide from God. They
did not want to see or to be seen by God. They found, as many have since, that the eyes of the Lord are in
every place, and that he that covereth his sins shall not prosper (Proverbs 15:3; Proverbs 28:13).
Where art thou? God seeks out the sinner. He cries, “Where art thou?” – a question which every single one
of us must answer in relation to his Lord. One of the most unique things man knows about God is His great love.
He takes the first step in seeking out the sinner. All through the Old Testament He tried to woo Israel back to
Himself, and in the New Testament, we learn that He sent His Son into the world to save sinners.
Adam tried to evade a direct answer to the question by using the excuse that he was naked, and so I hid
myself, but God got to the root of the trouble immediately by asking him how he knew he was naked. Adam had
never known this before. Not willing to accept all the blame, Adam said, The woman thou gavest … me, she
gave me … and I did eat. Adam blamed God and Eve for his sin. God asked Eve about her part in the sin, and
she laid the blame on the serpent. Both Adam and Eve put the blame for their acts upon another. God was not
blind as to where the guilt lay. Nor is He ever. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. And the Lord knoweth
them that are his. How true to human nature this lesson is! How we blame everyone except ourselves for the
condition we are in, for the sin we have committed. The game of “passing the buck” is as old as man himself.
God’s Hatred for Sin
Genesis 3:14 And the Lord God said…Because thou hast done this. No matter how much God may love
the sinner, He cannot let the sin go unpunished. God hates sin, and He is not satisfied until all sin is atoned for.
In verses 14-19 God pronounces curses upon the serpent, the woman, and the man, because they all had a part in
the sin against God. The punishments were: (1) to the serpent, a two-fold curse – it would be the lowest of the
animals, to go on its belly, to eat dust, to be at enmity with mankind and with Christ (seed of the woman), to
bruise his heel and be bruised on its head (a prophecy of Christ’s victory over Satan on the Cross); (2) to the
woman – pain and sorrow in childbearing, subjection to a husband; (3) to the man – a curse upon the ground so
it should grow weeds, thorns, and thistles. In the sweat of his face, he would work for a living. We see all of
these things today.

We can never picture too darkly the terribleness of sin, both in the heart of man and as it must look to the
eyes of a holy God. Sin is that evil nature in man which causes him to rebel against God, and which only the
transforming power of God in Christ can change.
Hope in the Midst of Despair
Genesis 3:15 And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed;
it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Here God becomes the first Prophet. He brings the
good news that through His Son, Jesus – the seed of the woman, no earthly father – He had a perfect plan for
bringing mankind, who was dead in sin, life again. The enmity between the seed of the devil and seed of the
woman became more intense with each age. Do we see it today? Here is a prophecy of the victory of Christ.
Thus at the very beginning of history, we find this promise and hope, not only in the victory to be gained by
Christ over sin, but also the real assurance that mankind through Christ may continually win over temptation.
Victory over sin is assured for the saint by Christ’s victory on the Cross. By His strength, we are more than
conquerors. When temptations come with overwhelming power, we can by Christ’s help defeat them.
Man Separated From the Tree of Life
Genesis 3:22-24 Lest he…take also of the tree of life … Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from
the garden. God in His love protected man from the fate of living forever in this sinful state. The Tree of Life
had not been forbidden before sin came, but now its eating would be tragic. So He drove out the
man…placed…Cherubim’s, and a flaming sword which turned every way. This might be named “Paradise
Lost” in the first Adam. But thank God for the last Adam, Jesus Christ! Through Him was Paradise regained.
Through Christ and His victory over sin and death, the way of the Tree of Life is once more opened to man.
The cruse has been lifted, and we who believe on Christ become heirs of His eternal salvation. Read Revelation
2:7 and Revelation 22:2.
JUST A THOUGHT
To neglect doctrine and rely upon spirituality to keep
the church strong is soon to lose spirituality also.

The Nature of Sin
Scripture Texts: Romans 5:12; James 1:13-15; Isaiah 59:2;
John 8:34; 1 John 3:8
Sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4). There is
sin of conduct – of acts – what we do or leave undone. There is
sin of character – of being – what we are. All unrighteousness
is sin (1 John 5:17). The sinful character or nature is the cause
of choosing to sin. Sinful acts spring from sin in the heart. We
can also be guilty of sin without committing the act. The wish
to is sin. By approving of or taking pleasure in other people’s
sins, we become guilty of them.
All have sinned. Because all have sinned, all need a Savior.
Sin always brings death. Sin separates us from God, makes us
children of the devil and will finally take us to hell.
Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to
any people (Proverbs 14:34).
MEMORY VERSE: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished,
bringeth forth death.—James 1:15
The Great Curse
Romans 5:12 By one man sin entered. Adam and Eve, by their act of disobedience, brought sin into the
world. This thing they had brought upon the human race was the greatest curse of mankind, in fact, the only
curse. Adam’s sin brought sin and death to all mankind. Death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.
We are not punished for Adams sin, but Adam’s sin gave us the tendency to yield to sin. All people have done
so. Then we each suffer the consequences of our own sins. If we could only weigh more carefully the effects of
our every act! Because we all have sinned, none excepted; so all have this death, none excepted; therefore, all
need the Savior, none excepted.
Lust Bringeth Forth Sin
James 1:13-15 God does not send temptation to sin. Temptation is the suggestion in our minds. It is caused
by our lust. Lusts are normal desires, twisted and corrupted by sin. Lust is the wish which draws us away from
God and toward sin. We listen and look and think about the sin, and then temptation appears upon the scene. We
yield. The lust bringeth forth sin: and sin … bringeth forth death. Death is separation from God. It is a dark
picture, getting blacker at every step – evil, sorrow, fear, and finally, hell forever. The devil tells us there is no
harm, but he is a liar (John 8:44). On the path away from God, things always grow worse, never better. We all
are on it until saved by Jesus Christ.
Sinners Need God
Isaiah 59:2 Your iniquities have separated between you and your God. Separation – death. No
communion with God, no smile from Him, no strength through Him, no answer to prayer from Him, and no
hope of being with Him. Sin separates and must be cleared away before the contact is made again. Jesus died to
clear it away. He is the one mediator between God and men (1 Timothy 2:5), the only One Who can make the
connection.

Like a flower craves sunshine, so the heart of man craves God and cannot be satisfied without Him. The
breath of God made man a living soul and gave him holiness, truth, love, light, and life. Sin cut off man from
these. Sinners are always wandering in the darkness of death, starving for God and never satisfied. The devil
pictured the tree as good, pleasant, and to be desired. What a lie that was! A child asked to be told the story of
the poison tree. He named it right. God is the only One Who can heal man of the poison. Jesus, God’s Son, died
to do it. He tells us, Beside me there is no Saviour (Isaiah 43:11).
Sin Enslaves
John 8:34 Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. Sin blinds, sin binds, and sin enslaves. Sinners
may say, “I have sin under control in my life. I am not going to do this and that.” The entire time one thinks he
has sin in his life under control; he is being wound more tightly in its entangling web. No sinner can truthfully
say he is a free person. What he would not, that he does, and what he would do, he cannot. Continually fighting
continually defeated. The binding, enslaving power of sin is the reason for the failure of some to yield to Christ,
even when they hear the Gospel and desire to break with sin. There is one way to freedom, found in John 8:36.
Sin corrupts the heart until every imagination of the thoughts is evil continually (Genesis 6:5). It twists the
conscience until man can do wrong and excuses it, or chooses wrong with no sorrow. Sin changes the affections
until people love self rather than God. It sets the affections on earthly things. The more we love material gifts
that perish, the less we love the Giver. Sin enslaves the will under the control of the devil until man is no longer
free in the choice of right, but his will is over-balanced toward the choice of evil. Men loved darkness rather
than light (John 3:19). Sin is unjust; it causes the innocent to suffer for others’ acts. There is nothing right
about sin. God hates sin so much that He made a way of escape in Christ. That which God hates, the saints hate
too. Sin keeps a person from God and Heaven. Read 1 Corinthians 6:9-10. Why do people remain in sin when
they are shown an escape route through the Gospel? It is because of this enslavement of the will. Sin binds.
The Cure for Sin
1 John 3:8 He that committeth sin is of the devil. The sinner is not of God. He follows the devil. He is like
the devil. He belongs to the devil. He is a child of the devil. The devil did a destructive work in Eden. All
wrong, sickness, suffering, and death came in then. The place of the sinner is in the devil’s kingdom, in the
devil’s family. Is there hope for the sinner? Yes. God has not left man to remain the helpless captive of sin. He
has a plan to save him. That way is the Son of God who was manifested, that He might destroy the works of
the devil. Thank the Lord!
To have life of soul, we must get rid of sin from both actions and heart. Reformation of habits – “turning
over a new leaf” from evil doings to good works – is not the cure. The soul is dead because of sins committed
within. Therefore, we must be made new inside, born again of God. This can be done only through faith in the
blood of Jesus Christ.

Building boys is better than mending men.

GOD’S GRACE EXAMINED
Scripture Texts: 2 Corinthians 8:9; Ephesians 2:4-10;
Ephesians 4:7
Grace is unmerited love and favor, the mercy of God or
benefits His mercy imparts, and the life of God flowing to
man. Grace, to work, requires two; it is the giving of
unearned good from one to another.
Salvation cannot be earned. It is received through faith
by God’s grace. Grace is the free gift of God’s life or His virtue, which because of His love He gives to those
who need it and believe in Him. Christ died for us while we were sinners. We had done and could do nothing to
save ourselves or to deserve help. Also, the saved person cannot continue to live holy in his own strength. We
need help. God gives it by grace. We have only to take it. God has an abundant supply.
MEMORY VERSE: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.
—Ephesians 2:8
Who Can Have Grace?
2 Corinthians 8:9 The rich …became poor in order that the poor might be rich. An unequal exchange!
This is not just. No, much more. It is the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.
One may say, “I do not think a wicked criminal SHOULD be forgiven.” No, not SHOULD. If he should be,
if he deserved it, it would be justice, not grace. But if he comes repenting to Jesus, owning that he does not
deserve it, God will forgive him anyway. That is grace. God gives what we DO NOT deserve, when He
SHOULD NOT. The greater the sin, the more grace pours out from Gods love to cover it. Justice would damn us
all. God’s grace is unmeasured.
We Cannot Earn Salvation
Ephesians 2:4-7 - It is hard to define grace because there is nothing else like it. But rich in mercy, for his
great love comes pretty close to describing it. When we were dead in sins … (Compare Romans 5:8). Only
God loves like this. Giving what is not deserved or earned, what we are not fit for – that is grace. To earn
salvation is impossible. If we think we deserve God’s favor because of position, respectability, living a good
life, working hard, suffering a lot, making sacrifices, raising a family, being a good neighbor, or anything else of
our own, we cannot be saved. There is something for us to do, but it is only to clear the way for salvation, never
to earn it. What goodness could pay for the smallest sin, when constant sinlessness is the requirement?
Raised us up – What a great raising – from death to life, to heavenly places in Christ Jesus, not only with
Him, but in Him. Where Jesus is, it is Heaven there. This can be understood only by experiencing it. In the ages
to come – throughout the generations when the church shall grow, prosper, and be victorious until Jesus comes
back, and then beyond this life, in Heaven. His kindness continues to give the exceeding riches of his grace,
and all through Christ Jesus.
GRACE AND FAITH
Ephesians 2:8-9 “Saved by grace” and “”saved by faith” are often used to express the same thought, that the
dependence must be upon God to do the working of saving. In this verse we see the different place which each –
grace and faith occupies. It is by grace … through faith. The faith of the person causes Him to reach his hand;
the grace of God causes Him to place the gift of salvation in it. We are saved by grace on God’s part and by faith

on the part of man. Not of yourselves – If it were of ourselves, it would not be of grace. Grace means the giving
of something good from one to another. What anything has of itself cannot be of grace. Not of works. It is tragic
that so many people are trying to work their way to God when He has never reached that way. If salvation could

Ephesians 2:10 His workmanship – Whatever of good is in God’s people or is accomplished by them is
done by God. When we are created in Christ Jesus, that is, made alive in Him, born again, it is unto good
works, or for the purpose of doing good. If any believe that the fact of grace leaves us free to commit sin, this
verse shows their mistake. Saved people are not sinners. God hath before ordained – it was His original plan –
that we should walk in them – good works. If we do not, how can we claim to be living in His grace? We are
then refusing it. Read Philippians 2:13.
But what is faith? Faith gives substance to things hoped for (Hebrews 11:1). Faith rests on belief, but it is
more than belief. It is belief in action. Faith is belief which leads us to step forward and lay hold on what God
has promised. The well-known hymn expresses it perfectly: “Just as I am, without one plea, But that Thy blood
was shed for me, And that Thou bid’st me come to Thee, O Lamb of God I come, I come.”
The Grace Fits the Gift
Ephesians 4:7 But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
Grace is measured by the gift Christ gives us for service in His church. Read the context. When He gives the gift
of prophecy, He gives the grace needed to be a prophet. When one is called to be a teacher, He gives the grace
needed for teaching. The wisdom, strength, abilities, patience, and love given are measured by the demands
made upon the life. God has a good supply of grace. Call for it. Sometimes we use it up very fast. We are saved
by grace, not our own powers. Sometimes we face our holy calling with apprehension, dread, and fear, knowing
we have no ability to live the life or to do the work He lays before us. Truly, we have not. But God tells us, If
any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God that giveth…and it shall be given him (James 1:5). We need
only to hold up our cup to Him, our earthen vessel. Read 2 Corinthians 4:7. Into it He pours grace. He pours as
much as we need, as much as our faith will take in.
Many try to live the Christian life in their own strength. They try and fail, then try again, but never reach a
victorious life. We must cease striving in our own strength and let Him do the work.
The story is told of a man who said to D.L. Moody, “I would like to come to Christ, but sin has me chained
and I cannot.” “Why don’t you come, chains and all?” asked Mr. Moody. The man did, and Christ broke every
chain. We do not cease to need grace when saved. Every day we need God’s grace to give us power to live holy,
to give wisdom, to use us, and to produce the fruit of the Spirit.

Salvation is a gift, not a payment.

AN EXAMPLE OF GOD’S GRACE
Scripture Text: Luke 7:36-50
Today we study one of the many instances when Jesus, while
on earth, saved a sinner. A sinful woman showed her repentance
and her faith in Jesus by washing His feet with tears, wiping them
with her hair, and anointing them with ointment. It was not
goodness or works that earned salvation from sin for the woman.
Jesus forgave her by grace, or as a free gift. He will still do the
same for any person who repents and believes in Him.
Possibly the woman had heard Jesus preach and had been
thrilled by His assurance of forgiveness for the sinner. The religious
leaders made it quite evident that they considered such as she to be
accursed and eternally alienated from God. Probably the woman felt
she could get nearer to Jesus at the feast than she could in the
temple, as He was preaching.
MEMORY VERSE: But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound.—Romans 5:20b
An Uninvited Guest
Luke 7:36-38 We are told that at an Oriental feast, anyone is perfectly free to enter the dining room while
the feast is in progress, but he is to occupy one of the seats over against the wall. Woman … which was a
sinner – She was bad, lost, in need, and because of sin, could not help herself. She boldly pressed into the
banquet hall on this occasion, carrying with her an expensive bottle filled with precious ointment. At his feet
behind him weeping … wash his feet with tears … wipe … with … hairs … kissed his feet … anointed.
Does not this speak of a deep attitude of the heart, of confession, of sorrow, of repentance, of love and gratitude?
No doubt she had bought the perfume with which the bottle was filled for the purpose of anointing her own body
and increasing her seductiveness. Her new life now indicated a new and exalted use for this ointment. It had
been bought for an evil purpose; it was now dedicated to a heavenly purpose. As her tears fell upon the Master’s
feet, she unloosed her hair – a shameful thing for an Oriental woman to do in public – and wiped the tears from
Jesus’ feet. That hair which had probably been a chief factor in her evil attractiveness was now dedicated to the
glorious use of wiping the Master’s feet.
Luke 7:39 When the Pharisee … saw it, he spake within himself. But Simon was deaf to all of this. He
thinks his life is blameless. He is so indifferent to the plight of the woman that he makes himself an even worse
sinner than the person he scorns. He thought that she had no right to touch Jesus. What he did not know was the
love of God. He did not know why Jesus came to earth. Where there is no right, no merit, there grace can work.
Simon was attracted to Jesus, yet not enough to become a disciple. He was conscious of the woman’s sin, but
not of his own. Simon’s sin was eating at his soul like a cancer, and he was entirely unaware of it.
Simon was a Pharisee who kept the ceremonies of the Law. He was respectable. He made a dinner to honor
Jesus. He knew he was not guilty of such sins as this woman. Therefore, there was no sorrow for sin in his heart.
The woman knew she was bad. She also knew that Jesus was good. In her heart was a longing for such
goodness. Her longing, mixed with sorrow for her sins, caused her to act. Blessed are they which do hunger
and thirst after righteousness for they shall be filled (Matthew 5:6). She hungered. She was filled. Simon
hungered not. He was left empty.
Our Lord’s Rebuke

Luke 7:40-46 Jesus knowing of Simon’s criticism tells a parable of two debtors. One owed much, one
little, but both were treated alike – forgiven. All sinners, big or little, need forgiveness. All have nothing to pay.
Much forgiveness brings much love. Simon loved God little because he had no sense of divine deliverance from
sin. The woman’s sins had been many, but she had forsaken them, and God had forgiven them. She could not
describe the change in her being. She could only show forth great love, appreciation, and joy for the One Who
had brought to pass this glorious work of God’s grace.
Salvation is always given on the same basis. That basis is God’s mercy and grace, not on what we deserve.
The greater debtor loved the most. The person with many sins was saved before the one with less. Virtue lies not
in sin, but in sorrow for sin, in repentance, in the transfer of dependence from oneself to Jesus Christ.
Jesus rebuked His host for his poor manners. Simon had provided no water for the feet of Jesus, a courtesy
extended to dinner guests when they entered the house; but the sinful woman had washed the feet of Jesus with
her tears and wiped them with her hair. Had Simon been greeting another Pharisee, he would have embraced
him and kissed him; but Jesus had not been considered worthy of such honor. Yet the woman had covered the
feet of Jesus with her kisses. Simon had failed to anoint the head of his Guest with oil – a courtesy which no one
trained in the etiquette of that time would have neglected in receiving a guest of any distinction – yet the woman
had anointed Jesus’ feet not with oil, but with precious ointment. Christianity involves good manners. In the
brotherhood of Christ, discrimination between persons shows disrespect to God.
Forgiveness and Peace
Luke 7:47-50 As Jesus contrasts Simon’s and the woman’s treatment of Jesus, we are reminded of His
words in Luke 5:32, I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. That is grace. How mercy
must have leaped and shouted against justice at the outpouring of grace when Jesus said, Her sins, which are
many, are forgiven. Praise God!
The Pharisees murmured within themselves, “Who is this that forgiveth sins also?” This should have
convinced them that Jesus was God’s Messiah. Jesus said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in
peace. It was not her love that saved her, but her faith. Her love had opened her heart and allowed faith to bring
in God’s grace. The woman gave Jesus three precious things – repentance, faith, and love. He gave her three
divine gifts in return – forgiveness, salvation, and peace. She walked now into the heavenly realms of life and
light. She was at peace with God, with her own soul, and with the world.
JUST A THOUGHT
To be ready to die is to be ready to live.

LESSON 12
SONS OF GOD
Scripture Text: 1 John 3:1-10
We have seen that God’s salvation redeems us from the curse which sin brought upon man. Many and varied
are the teachings concerning sin and its removal. As in every consideration, the Bible answer is the final one.
Today we look into man’s position in regards to sin, God, and the devil.
If God saves us without our works, does it mean we can go on sinning and still be saved? No! Since God
supplies power to live holy lives, He requires that kind of living. God’s people are holy. Sinners are the devil’s
children. There is a plain line of division between the two. Let us see what the Bible plainly states as to the
difference between God’s children and the devil’s children.
MEMORY VERSE: Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God
through Christ.—Galatians 4:7
Two Kinds of People
1 John 3:1 Behold, what manner of love – Such love we cannot comprehend, we can only behold, taste,
and accept. What has it done? It has made us to be called the sons of God, made of His family. The world
(unsaved people) knoweth us not, which probably explains the reason for the many ideas concerning what a
child of God is and should be like. The world knew him not – knew not God – and so cannot understand His
people, for they are like God. The world and sons of God are different, separate.
1 John 3:2 Now are we – in this life – here we must be made children of God, if at all. The next life holds
even greater blessings of which we are not now fully told. Read Romans 8:17. What a precious privilege!
1 John 3:3 This hope of Heaven’s blessings causes one to purify himself, or to throw away the filthy habits
of life which he has picked up along the way. Why? Because only the pure can enter there. (See Matthew 5:8).
How pure? Even as He is pure.
1 John 3:4-5 Sin is anything contrary to God’s Law. He was manifested, or Christ came to take away our
sins. Not to leave us in them, nor gloss over, nor sweep them under a rug, nor shut His eyes to them, but to take
them away. God never requires anything but that He, by His grace, makes it possible. Christ provided for the
removal of sin.
One of the facts standing out plainly here is that there are two kinds of people – saints and sinners, children
of God and children of the devil. The children of God shall be like him, are pure even as he is pure, are
righteous even as he is righteous, do not commit sin, and are born of God. The children of the devil sin, are
of the devil, are not of God, and love not their brothers. Each kind of person is known by his life, whether or not
it is righteous. The dividing line is definite. The reason the dividing lines are laid so plainly before us is to show
us where we are standing, and to let us know a crossing is necessary if we are to be in God’s family, the Church
of God.
This is God’s statement. It tells us not that God’s people SHOULD BE holy, but that His people ARE holy.
If it has not appeared so to us, it may be that we have been confusing church membership with the experience of
rebirth – heart purity.
Righteousness Is of God
1 John 3:6 Whosoever abideth in Him sinneth son – No question as to the meaning of this. Our part is to
abide, to remain in Him. He will keep us from sinning. This is one part of purifying oneself (verse 3). Sinners
have not seen or known Him.
1 John 3:7 Even as he is righteous – That is the true Bible standard. Holiness is a reasonable standard. The
world expects it, although probably not conscious that it is holiness. That is why they criticize sinning church

The Seed of God
1 John 3:8 He that committeth sin is of the devil. No sinful person or organization belongs to God. The
Son of God was manifested to destroy the works of the devil. Either Christ has the victory over sin in man, or
His coming was a failure. It was no failure. What good news for all captive souls!
1 John 3:9 Whosoever is born of God does not commit sin. A clear statement as in verse 8, but on the
other side of the question. This draws a definite and wide line between God’s people and Satan’s. Cannot sin –
not that anyone in the world gets where it is impossible to sin. Experience shows that anyone choosing to sin can
do so. Sometimes it is the one who has been a child of God for a number of years. But no one can sin while the
seed of God remaineth in him. God and sin cannot be in a person at the same time. When God comes in, sin
goes out; when sin comes in, God goes out. Life’s greatest tragedy is for God to leave a heart and life for sin to
take over.
1 John 3:10 Again, that clear separation between the children of God … and the children of the devil.
This shows the falsity of Modernism’s claim that are people are brothers, all children of God. What is the
difference in them? In whether or not they do righteousness and have love, the love of God. Right actions are
the difference which marks them outwardly to the eyes of their fellowmen. The inner difference lies in whether
or not they are born of God, made alive in Christ Jesus, have the seed of God within.
Settle the Question
1 John 1:8 and 10 are sometimes used to ob ject to the p ossib ility of holy living. Remember verse 9 is
between them and solves the problem, if there be a problem. If we say that we have no sin – to be cleansed
from, or that we have not sinned, we are not saying or acting according to truth. We are making God a liar, for
He has declared that all have sinned (Romans 3:23). Such a one is trying to cover his sins, and of such, God
says that he shall not prosper – not meaning financially, but in spiritual prosperity. We must acknowledge our
sin, but we must not remain in it. Frank confession brings forgiveness and cleansing from God. This makes one
holy.
Do not argue for sin or seek to excuse it or to avoid its removal. Sin brought every sorrow this world has
ever known. Its cure is the greatest blessing ever given to the world. Christ is the cure. He is coming again. Be
diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless (2 Peter 3:14).
JUST A THOUGHT
Store your mind with Scripture.
It is food for your soul.

LESSON 13
THE PERFECT MAN
Scripture Texts: Ephesians 1:4; 1 Peter 1:15-16; 1 John 1:9;
Romans 6:11-14; Romans 8:1-2
To live holy is to live perfect lives in the eyes of God. Because
some fail to see the difference between Christian perfection and human
perfection, they fail to see the need of living holy before God. The
Church of God is a perfect people, made free from sin and acceptable
to God.
Since holiness is so necessary that no one can see the Lord
without it, we must know how to become holy and remain perfect in
the eyes of God. Every repentant sinner who comes to Christ will be
cleansed from sin, made holy. He is kept holy by the grace of God and
his own care in using his faculties for righteous living. It is our
responsibility to accept and use the grace given us. Full dedication of
ourselves and our all to God brings the Holy Spirit to guide us on our
way. This is the way one is made holy and kept perfect every day.
MEMORY VERSE: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father
which is in heaven is perfect.—Matthew 5:48
Perfection is Necessary
Ephesians 1:4 He hath chosen us … before the foundation of the world to be holy. The holiness, or
perfection, of man has been Gods plan from the first. It was not added afterward. Holiness is perfection,
perfection is holiness. Man will always be prone to make human error, but human error is not sin and cannot
spoil one’s perfect life in Christ.
1 Peter 1:15-16 God’s family is one. His children are born of Him and must be like Him. Refer to Memory
Verse, also, 2 Corinthians 13:11; Colossians 1:28; Colossians 4:12. Holiness is of such great necessity that no
man shall see the Lord without it (Hebrews 12:14). One unforgiven sin will spoil our perfection.
An often-heard remark is, “No one is perfect.” No, not perfect regarding mistakes, but yes, perfect regarding
sins. Another remark that is often heard is, “Practice makes perfect. No, this is not so in the case of perfect
living. Obedience to Christ does. Jesus said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and … do as I say unto you
(Matthew 19:21). Sins are done from wrong motives, knowing it is wrong, with a disregard for God’s will.
They range from criminal action to carelessness in discharging duties, but guilt is attached to them all. Mistakes
may bring undesirable results but never guilt.
Perfection Can Be Attained
1 John 1:9 If we confess our sins – Real confession begins in the heart – owning to ourselves that we are
guilty. It goes on to outward expression – owning to others that we have sinned. It is not satisfied until all
possible is done to right those wrongs. God meets the repentant sinner with forgiveness and cleansing by the
blood of Christ. He cleanses from all unrighteousness – all that is contrary to God. When that is done, the
person is perfect, free from sin.
Romans 6:11-13 When a repentant sinner comes to Christ, he dies to sin and self, is separated from them.
Then he is resurrected, made alive unto God, or joined to Him. It is important for each saved one to realize this
and at all times to consciously reckon himself dead to sin and alive unto God. Being awake to his position in
Christ, he is better prepared to hold it. For, although it all comes through Jesus Christ our Lord, we still have

freedom of will, and we have a part in keeping ourselves free from sin. Depending upon God, we must say no to
sin and lust. We must not yield our members – our hands, feet, eyes, tongues, minds, etc. – to be used as tools of
sin. On the other hand, we are to yield them to God to use as He wills. We are free to yield or withhold.
Withholding is sin. When fully yielded to Him, they will be put to use in His service. They will not be idle.
Romans 6:14 Sin shall not have dominion over you – not rule you. The sinner is under the power of sin.
He is not free. Sin does the ruling. But Christ breaks sin’s power. Read John 8:36. Christ saves him by grace,
and then puts him under grace for all the future. The saint has the power of God at his disposal for living
victoriously over sin. This is another fact he should realize very clearly. Being constantly conscious of it, he will
continually depend upon God and draw upon Him for victory over trial and temptation which Satan is sure to
send.
A People Not Condemned
Romans 8:1-2 There is therefore now no condemnation. There is a people who are not condemned – no
blame, no guilt, no accusation from God. They live perfect lives. How do they do it? They are in Christ Jesus.
They are born again, made alive, transferred from Satan’s kingdom to Christ’s. They are still in the flesh; they
live here on earth just as other people, eating, sleeping, working, but they do not walk … after the flesh. They
do not follow the lusts of the flesh. They do not live to please themselves, but God. Their eyes are looking
toward Heaven, not Earth. They are living for eternity, not for this world. They walk after the Spirit. The Holy
Spirit directs their lives. The Spirit frees them from the law of sin and death. The law of the Spirit of life in
Christ Jesus frees them. No one should even try to live a perfect life without the Holy Spirit in his heart. Of
course, it cannot be done.
Our hearts can be perfectly clean, our motives perfectly pure, the love of our hearts perfectly set upon God.
What we do may not be much, but it can be pure all through. It must be to meet God’s approval. We all are weak
and make many mistakes. This is why God has not left perfection depending upon our own strength, but upon
His. Lean on Him more.
Some Theories About Perfection
All agree that sin is bad and that it should be conquered in some measure by some method. A few theories
are: (1) That we are bound to sin every day but should seek forgiveness. There are two flaws in this: (a) We
might die in an unforgiven moment. (b) Continual sinning dulls the conscience and repentance wanes. (2) That
God imputes Christ’s righteousness to His children’s account while they go on sinning. (a) This would leave no
difference between saints and sinners. (b) It would take away man’s right of choice, would be artificial. God not
only counts Christ’s righteous to us, He actually makes it ours (2 Corinthians 5:21). (3) That we can sin and be
purged of it at some future time or place. Since the Bible mentions no such opportunity, it is fatal to trust in it.
(4) That there are two kinds of sin, one bad and the other not so bad; one will damn the soul, and the other will
not. (a) God recognizes no such division. (b) It would be impossible to place borderline sins in the correct
division. God has the best way. It is to create us in righteousness and true holiness (Ephesians 4:24).
JUST A THOUGHT
Adam and Eve committed only one sin.
